correctness.rationale: For the row generator the zero row sums give the stationary root, the negative trace is a+b+c+h, and the three principal 2×2 minors are ab, ac, and (b+h)c. Setting x=h+a+b−c gives the quadratic discriminant x²−4ab, so the complex band is (h_−,h_+) intersected with h≥0. It is nonempty exactly at c>c_0 and has a strictly positive onset exactly at c>(sqrt(a)+sqrt(b))². At equality in the latter condition there is a defective point at h=0 rather than a nonempty initial real phase. At a nonnegative double root λ<0, semisimplicity would imply Q=λ(I−1π), contradicting Q_02=0 and π_2>0. Flux balance sets bπ_1=cπ_2=aπ_0−hπ_1; normalizing yields J=abc/[ab+ac+c(b+h)] with strictly negative derivative. On the band ρ²=(4ab−x²)/(x+2c)² has derivative −4(cx+2ab)/(x+2c)³. Its only turning point is h_*=c−a−b−2ab/c. When positive, c>c_1>sqrt(ab) puts it strictly inside the band and substitution yields ρ²=ab/(c²−ab). When c_0<c≤c_1, h=0 lies in the band and is the unique maximum, including the stationary-derivative case at c=c_1; at c≤c_0 the zero-extension is identically zero. Starting at state 0 the complex transient has a nonzero cosine coefficient 1−π_0, hence infinitely many sign crossings, whereas an exponential times a constant plus one exponential or a linear term has at most one. The supplied verify_cycle.py and its verification notes report algebra and sampled checks; no supplied script was executed. The independent algebra covers boundary cases that sampling cannot certify.
